India congratulates the French Presidency on its stewardship of the Security Council and thanks the Secretary-General and the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) for their respective briefings and statements. India reiterates that it is neither a signatory to the Rome Statute nor a member of the ICC.

The trajectory of the Ukraine conflict remains profoundly concerning, with the future outlook increasingly disturbing. The impact is being felt globally, with soaring costs and acute shortages in food grains, fertilizers and fuel. The global South, in particular, is experiencing this pain acutely. Therefore, India strongly emphasizes the need for an immediate cessation of hostilities, a return to dialogue and diplomacy, and avoiding measures that may further complicate an already struggling global economy.

While India continues to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and economic support to our neighbours, we also have a responsibility to address other critical issues. As the United Kingdom just stated, there have been horrific acts of violence and atrocities committed by Russian forces against civilians in Ukraine, including those in Izyum. However, we recently drew the Council's attention to the killings in Bucha and other places, where Ukrainian forces have been confirmed to have committed crimes against humanity. Where such acts occur, whether by Russian or Ukrainian forces, it is imperative that they be investigated in an objective and independent manner, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations. That was our position regarding the Bucha incident, and we supported calls for an independent investigation at that time. Today, we call for extreme caution, fairness, due process and due diligence in any action taken.

With respect to the draft resolution annexed to the Council's agenda, the dossier does not currently establish India's endorsement or a recorded vote on the measure. The document does not reflect the final position of India. We review all matters carefully before forming a final view. We urge the Secretary-General to provide additional information and clarify certain aspects, including those relating to the ICC, so that the Council may make an informed decision. Politics should never provide cover to evade accountability or facilitate impunity, but all actions must be fair, objective and in line with international norms.

The need of the hour is to end the war in Ukraine and return to the negotiating table. The Security Council must continue to live up to its purpose as the premier forum for diplomacy. After we address the war in Ukraine, we must also ensure that other threats to international peace and security, including terrorism, are effectively dealt with. That is why India strongly emphasized yesterday that there cannot be victors or vanquished in the fight against terrorism.<|im_end|>

The United Kingdom congratulates the Secretary-General on his clear account of the suffering caused by Russia's invasion of Ukraine. We thank the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court for his report detailing the ongoing atrocities and calls for accountability. As the UK emphasized in our recent statements, Russia's attack continues, with horrific reports of civilian suffering, including the recent discovery of many Ukrainian soldiers and civilians killed and raped in Izyum. We reject in the strongest terms Russian claims of impunity for crimes against humanity.

The United Kingdom also drew the Council's attention to Russia's attempts to expand its illegal gains. With the ongoing war preventing a return to diplomacy, sham referendums held in Ukrainian territories provide a false guise for annexation. As the UK made clear earlier, we unequivocally reject any changes to Ukraine's territory by force and will not recognize any results of those referendums.

The UK understands that the United States will submit a draft resolution condemning the referendums, calling for non-recognition and a Russian withdrawal. The United Kingdom will engage constructively with that draft. Other claims made by the French presidency and the United States regarding the nature of the proceedings are noted but do not constitute commitments by the United Kingdom.

India reminded the Council that it is not a party to the Rome Statute and provided context on its position regarding the ICC. That position remains unchanged.

More broadly, the pros and cons of continuing the war are clear. The United Kingdom has been a leading provider of humanitarian and economic aid to both Ukraine and our European neighbours. We remain committed to supporting Ukraine in its defence against unprovoked aggression. The hour demands an end to the bloodletting and a path to peace.<|im_end|>
